newsitem.title: USA: Government to seek bacteria-tainted blood.
newsitem.headline: Government to seek bacteria-tainted blood.

text.p: Federal health officials said Thursday they will study the extent to which blood used in transfusions is contaminated with potentially deadly bacteria.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said 29 people are known to have died from bacterial contamination of blood products between 1986 and 1991, but the agency suspects the actual figure is higher.
"No national surveillance system for bacterial contamination of blood products exists in the United States," CDC epidemiologist Dr. Matt Kuehnert said.

"The study that we're doing will look at all transfusion reactions," he said. "What we'd like to do is a national study that looks at the rate of transfusion reactions due to bacterial contamination."

At least five people have died since 1991 from blood products contaminated with Yersinia enterocolitica, a bacterium found in soil, water and animals that has sickened people who consumed contaminated oysters, fish, tofu or milk.

"There certainly are infections that are emerging in this country and in the world that we need to be vigilant about," Kuehnert said. "Although donors may be without symptoms on the day of donation their blood can transmit bacteria including Yersinia and recipients of that blood may develop fatal reactions."
